lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
recommendations-main.js: 1 file, 3,365,336 B, and 3 chunks of 175,913 B its runtime loads later, of which recommendations-main.js is 3,365,336 B (95.0 %).
recommendations-dashboard.js: 1 file, 3,360,640 B, and 3 chunks of 175,913 B its runtime loads later, of which recommendations-dashboard.js is 3,360,640 B (95.0 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,642,025 B in 246 modules, 48.8 % of the static path of recommendations-main.js, imported by its root in components/RecommendedFile.vue (useFormatDateTime) and components/Settings.vue (NcCheckboxRadioSwitch). It is imported per module as well, through 2 other specifiers.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

82 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 238,298 B, 7.1 % of the static path of recommendations-dashboard.js, next to 3 components the source names and 16 those pull in.
NcAppSidebar 15,945 B, NcRichContenteditable 13,061 B, NcModal 10,430 B, NcCollectionList 9,687 B, NcAppNavigationItem 9,035 B, NcContent 8,716 B, and 76 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.
